clue.text: Rare aversion concerning woman with dog

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for concerning or about
a pug is a small breed of dog
Nancy is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman and her dog are the object of someone's unusual dislike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare' belongs to the definition: the word is now seldom used, so it is a rare way of saying aversion. The charade runs in answer order, the dog before the woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Repugnancy is an old, little-used synonym for repugnance, a strong dislike or disgust.

clue.text: Absorbed — and made into a parcel, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the word is taken as spoken, by its sound

parts.note: something made into a parcel has been wrapped

explanation.surface: Someone engrossed while their goods are bundled up.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt means wholly engrossed, as when a reader is absorbed in a book.

clue.text: Cut up over airport concealing current contamination

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places the first piece above the next
in a down answer, up means the word for cut reads from the bottom

parts.note: to lop is to cut off, as with branches

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the airport surrounds the letter for current

parts.note: Luton is an airport north of London
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Pollution over an airport, made worse by cuts and hidden currents.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollution is the fouling of air, water or land by harmful substances.

clue.text: Unsocial work period solemn detectives change

parts.note: grave means serious or solemn
the Yard, Scotland Yard, is London's police headquarters, standing for its detectives
to shift is to change or move

explanation.surface: Serious detectives grumble about switching to awkward working hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A graveyard shift is a stint of work through the small hours of the night, cutting off social life.

clue.text: Turn up, dropping round primarily for church records

indicators.note: dropping one thing for another means a letter is swapped out for a new one

parts.note: to turn up is to arrive

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter of the word round

explanation.surface: Someone turns up at church, skipping the round, for its old records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping ... for' swaps one letter: the first letter of 'round' leaves the verb and the church abbreviation takes its place.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a collection of historical documents, or as a verb, to file records away.

clue.text: Rose to a high point, like some tits

definitions.meaning: reached the top, as a wave does at its peak
having a tuft of feathers on the head

explanation.surface: Some birds flew up to a perch on a summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A wave that has crested peaked, and a crested bird has a tufted head, as the crested tit does.

clue.text: Jewel a girl finally displayed after work

indicators.note: the letters that follow are placed after the work in the answer

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word girl is taken

explanation.surface: A girl shows off a jewel at the end of a working day.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is an iridescent gemstone, so it is a jewel.

clue.text: Composure one's discovered in American writer

indicators.note: discovered in means found inside, so the writer's name contains the pieces for one is

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer
one's stands for one is: I for one plus S

explanation.surface: An American author's calm manner is found in his work.
explanation.definitionFit: Poise is calm self-assurance and steadiness of manner, as composure is.

clue.text: Less demanding time for conveyance of cargo

parts.note: a lighter task is easier, less demanding
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An easier time is wanted for shipping goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighterage is moving goods between ship and shore in lighters, flat-bottomed barges, or the fee paid for it.

clue.text: Obscure military group reportedly qualified to arrest knight

indicators.note: to arrest means to hold, so the pieces close round the letter for knight

parts.note: a unit is a military group or detachment
N is the chess notation for knight

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word for qualified is taken by its sound

parts.note: eligible means qualified or entitled

explanation.surface: An unknown army squad, it is rumoured, is fit to detain a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone gives a spelling with a double L that 'qualified' never has; only the sound matters. 'Knight' is N in chess notation, since K is the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Unintelligible means impossible to understand, which is one sense of obscure.

clue.text: People with no following invited into old man's dance

indicators.note: invited into means welcomed inside, so the trimmed word for people goes within the word for father

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for one's father, the old man

indicators.note: with no tells us a letter is dropped from the word for people

parts.note: folk means people
f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A group of people is welcomed into a father's dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' is the abbreviation F, not a band of followers; once it goes, the rest of the word for people is put inside the father.
explanation.definitionFit: The polka is a lively Bohemian couple dance in two-four time.

clue.text: Constant inclination to take in son's washing

parts.note: c is the scientific symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

indicators.note: to take in means the word for inclination encloses the letter for son

parts.note: a leaning is an inclination or tendency
s is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone always inclined to take in their son's laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleansing is the act of making clean, which is what washing does.

clue.text: Outstanding hospital department engaging mean manager

indicators.note: engaging means holding within, so the first pair of pieces closes round the word for mean

parts.note: super means excellent or outstanding
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
to mean to do something is to intend it

explanation.surface: An excellent hospital department takes on a stingy boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like an adjective describing the manager, but it is the verb intend.
explanation.definitionFit: A superintendent is a person who oversees and directs an organisation or its work.

clue.text: Preacher abused Morse, upset about wrongdoing

indicators.note: abused means mistreated or misused, so the letters of Morse are rearranged
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the pieces read from the bottom

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a sin is a wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Inspector Morse, abused, is upset at some crime.
explanation.walkthrough: Morse is the TV detective Inspector Morse, but here his name is only letters to rearrange; 'upset' turns the two following pieces upside down together.
explanation.definitionFit: A sermoniser is someone who delivers sermons, so a preacher, often a moralising one.

clue.text: Old poem about Greek character backing Arab territory

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the poem is read in reverse

parts.note: rime is an archaic spelling of rhyme, a poem, as in The Rime of the Ancient Mariner

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the Greek letter is reversed

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An ancient poem about a Greek supporting an Arab land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses RIME to EMIR and 'backing' reverses ETA to ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An emirate is a state ruled by an emir, such as those of the Gulf.

clue.text: Piece of furniture employed in one theatre or another?

definitions.meaning: a sideboard with shelves for crockery

definitions.text: employed in one theatre or another?
definitions.meaning: a person who helps actors into costume in a playhouse, or one who applies bandages in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: Some item of furniture turns up on stage in more than one playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The second theatre is a hospital's operating theatre, where a surgeon's assistant who dresses wounds also has this title.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a kitchen cupboard with shelves and also the backstage helper who costumes performers.

clue.text: Most bad-tempered Italian brought up in county street

indicators.note: in means the reversed Italian sits inside the word for county

parts.note: a shire is an English county

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the word reads upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: The grumpiest Italian grew up on a county street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian' is It, Italian vermouth as in gin and It, a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Shirty is informal British for irritable or bad-tempered; this is its superlative.

clue.text: Like a simple song, perhaps, developing mostly nice mood

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means the word nice loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A pleasant mood grows, as in a plain little tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims NICE to NIC; 'developing' shuffles NIC with MOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Monodic describes monody, music for a single melodic line, which a simple song may be.

clue.text: Like some pasties — and grain, give or take

parts.note: corn is a cereal grain
ish is informal for roughly, give or take, as in six-ish

explanation.surface: Some pasties contain grain, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cornish pasty is a famous meat and vegetable pastry from Cornwall, in south-west England.

clue.text: Crooner once accepting bad position in publicity

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the crooner's name surrounds the word for bad

parts.note: Bing Crosby was a famous crooner of the past
ill means bad, as in ill will

explanation.surface: A former crooner tolerates being badly placed in advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: Billing is the order or prominence of performers' names on posters and advertisements.

clue.text: Support British pensioner abandoned by daughter

indicators.note: abandoned by means left without, so the letter for daughter is removed

parts.note: an oldster is an elderly person, a pensioner

explanation.surface: Help for a British pensioner whose daughter left her.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolster is to prop up or reinforce, and a bolster is also a long supporting pillow.

clue.text: Aerial display soldiers and sailors ultimately recall in dark periods

indicators.note: in means the following pieces sit inside the word for dark periods

parts.note: nights are the dark periods of each day
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers
the RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors collectively

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of the word recall

explanation.surface: Servicemen remember an air show during the war's darkest times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aerial display' suggests a flypast; it is a light show in the sky. 'sailors' stands for the Royal Navy as a body, with the article included.
explanation.definitionFit: The aurora borealis is a natural shimmering show of coloured lights high in the sky.

clue.text: Thick-skinned type playing horn around India

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the letter for India
playing means performing freely, so the letters of horn are rearranged

parts.note: India is the radio alphabet word for I

explanation.surface: A tough-hided musician plays the horn in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horn' fits the surface of a rhino perfectly, but here it is only letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros has a famously thick, armour-like hide.

clue.text: Half of capital Yankee invested in French city

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so the letter for Yankee goes into the half capital
half of means only the first three letters of the six-letter capital are kept

parts.note: London is the capital of the UK
Yankee is the radio alphabet word for Y

explanation.surface: An American puts half his capital into a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyon is France's third-largest city, on the Rhône and Saône rivers.

clue.text: Miser's second family to west of North Wales town

definitions.note: Miser's stands for miser is, the 's linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: in an across answer, west is to the left, so these letters come before the town

parts.note: kin means family or relatives
Flint is a town in North Wales

explanation.surface: A miser's alternative relatives live just west of a Welsh town.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinflint is a person who hates spending money, a tightwad.

clue.text: Brawny wartime fighting force unknown outside European capital

indicators.note: outside means the first pieces wrap round the letter that follows

parts.note: the BEF was the British Expeditionary Force of both world wars

indicators.note: capital means the first, or head, letter of the word European

parts.note: y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A muscular wartime army, of unknown strength, waits beyond a European capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European capital' suggests a city such as Paris, but it is just the letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefy means muscular and solidly built, as brawny does.

clue.text: Cross, and discourteous to listeners

indicators.note: to listeners means as heard, so the word for discourteous is taken by its sound

parts.note: rude means discourteous or impolite

explanation.surface: Someone is angry and impolite to the people listening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like the adjective angry; here it is the noun, a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is a crucifix, especially one set above the screen in a church.

clue.text: City man in underworld row accommodating in case

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so the ferryman surrounds the word for in case

parts.note: Charon is the ferryman who rows the dead over the Styx in the Greek underworld
lest means in case, for fear that

explanation.surface: A city man in a gangland quarrel is put up in a crate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a quarrel, but it is rowing a boat; the 'underworld' is Hades, not gangland.
explanation.definitionFit: Charleston is a port city in South Carolina, and also one in West Virginia.
